paras: The killing of William Broder was the shooting of a saloon keeper by vigilantes at Park Station, Montana Territory, on the night of June 15, 1882. Broder was called to the door of his saloon and shot dead, the vigilantes' stated reason being that his place was a resort for thieves. The news reached the wider press only as a one-sentence wire item, which Pacific coast dailies and Midwestern weeklies reprinted over the following two weeks.

According to a dispatch datelined Park Station on June 16, Broder was called to the door of his saloon "last night" by vigilantes and "riddled with bullets." The Sacramento Record-Union's news summary placed the killing on Thursday night and described Broder as "assassinated by vigilantes." The only reason given was the vigilantes' charge that the saloon was "the resort of thieves," an accusation the reports relayed without further detail. None of the reports names the vigilantes, gives their number or states Broder's race.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

On June 17 the dispatch ran in the Sacramento Daily Record-Union under the head "Assassination by Vigilantes," in the Eureka Daily Sentinel as "The Work of Vigilantes" and in the Los Angeles Herald as "Riddled with Bullets." The papers printed the vigilantes' reason as part of the report, adding no comment of their own. A condensed version, spelling the killers "vigilants," appeared in news-in-brief columns of the Mineral Point Tribune in Wisconsin on June 22 and the Barbour County Index in Kansas on June 29, the latter under the head "Riddled with Bullets."

chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: Vigilantes called Broder to his saloon door and shot him dead, giving as the reason that his place was a resort for thieves (A1, A3, A4).

Broder was killed by 'vigilantes' acting without legal authority on the stated ground that his saloon harbored thieves, a pretext of rough justice (A1, A3, A4); the number of vigilantes is not given, though the plural and the term imply a group (A1, A2).
Every report is the same June 16 Park Station wire dispatch or a condensation of it (A1, A3, A4, A5, A6); no independent local account was found.

accounts.label: Wire report
accounts.gist: A Park Station dispatch of June 16 said Broder was called to his saloon door the night before by vigilantes and riddled with bullets because his place was a resort for thieves.

framing.detail: Pacific coast dailies ran the dispatch under heads ranging from 'Assassination by Vigilantes' to 'Riddled with Bullets', relaying the vigilantes' reason without comment.
The Sacramento Record-Union's news summary used the word 'assassinated'.
